system.name: Pyrocumulus
system.one_liner: a SmartNIC-based hardware hypervisor that live-migrates storage-optimized VMs by intercepting and coordinating I/O without host CPU involvement

components.role: issues NVMe commands mediated by the FPGA

components.name: SmartNIC
components.role: FPGA-based hardware hosting the LM controller and network stack; boundary of this figure

components.name: LM Controller
components.role: generates LM-related send/receive commands and mediates VM access to local disks via a direct-access interface

components.name: n Emulated Host Queues
components.role: the full set of host-facing queues the LM controller emulates, split into regular VM queues and a dedicated LM queue

components.name: n-1 VM Queues
components.role: queues handling ordinary VM NVMe access

components.name: 1 LM Queue
components.role: dedicated queue for live-migration traffic, kept separate from ordinary VM queues

components.name: LM Module
components.role: groups the network-facing components handling migration traffic

components.name: Network Stack
components.role: sends/receives migration data over the network to/from the peer SmartNIC

components.name: Local Disk
components.role: NVMe storage attached to this host

components.name: n Disk Queues
components.role: per-disk command queues the LM controller issues NVMe commands through

flows.what: VM access: each NVMe command mediated by the FPGA before reaching the NVMe controller
VM access path continuing to local disk queues
LM double write: a write is duplicated into the LM queue for migration consistency
LM send (source): migration data sent out over the network stack
LM recv (dst): the destination SmartNIC receives migration data into its emulated host queues

content.key_idea: Pyrocumulus's FPGA SmartNIC emulates n host-facing queues (n-1 ordinary VM queues plus 1 dedicated LM queue) and a network stack, giving its LM controller full visibility to mediate VM NVMe access, double-write for consistency, and send/receive migration data directly between SmartNICs without host CPU involvement.
content.reading_order: Top-down on the left (VM into the LM controller's emulated queues, then to local disk queues via PCIe), with a branch right into the LM module/network stack for the numbered migration datapaths (1-4).

summary: Figure 4 is the internal architecture of Pyrocumulus's FPGA-based SmartNIC. An LM Controller emulates n host-facing queues, split into n-1 ordinary VM queues and 1 dedicated LM queue, and mediates every NVMe command between the VM and n Disk Queues on the Local Disk. Four numbered, color-coded datapaths run through this box: (1) ordinary VM access, mediated by the FPGA; (2) LM double write, duplicating writes into the LM queue for consistency; (3) LM send (source), pushing migration data out through the LM Module's Network Stack; and (4) LM recv (dst), the same network stack receiving migration data into a peer SmartNIC's emulated host queues. Because the LM controller sees all four paths, it can enforce consistency between ongoing VM I/O and in-flight migration I/O without involving the host CPU.
